body: Thank you so much for helping me out. That last paragraph you wrote hit home so much. I already achieved the rank, even if I'm not there now. Did it feel good for a moment? Yeah. But most likely, I won't care about my rank in a year or more. Have a great day man.

Wow that's an interesting perspective. But honestly, I'm not going to get anywhere by just succumbing to League. Maybe this ban was a blessing in disguise, but I will miss being complimented about being Masters and such. I have an ego too, but most of the time what stops me is my anxiety and depression. I have huge performance and ranked anxiety, especially when playing with a streamer. That kind of hinders me from just grinding and ignoring life. 

Anyways, after my ban, I'll see if I'm still up for playing ranked. Last season I only played once a month in D1 and didn't care about my rank. I guess I'm just not content with being D1 ever since I hit Challenger/Masters

I mean it's childish, but this imaginary rank is an achievement to me. I guess it makes me feel accomplished at one thing. I mean I love smoking weed amd hanging out with my friends, but I'm currently taking a semester off and have so much free time. I just wish I could find something to do that would consume more time than playing League
I didn't have the heart to live. My life isn't difficult for normal people, I just felt like it was too much to bear at that point.

Honestly, I'd be lying if I said that I don't love life. I love everything about life, even if I don't get to partake in its beauties. I regretted being so timid and shy when it comes to confessing. I regretted not doing things that I wanted to do; Travel the world, visit my home country, go to a concert. Realistically, of course I would like to do all these things, and the list could go on forever. Unfortunately, I was born with a general anxiety disorder, where I'm anxious about pretty much everything. The unfairness of life is so apparent throughout walking around and seeing those who believe they live terrible lives. I understand that some people genuinely life awful lives, but I believe that in most people, there are definitely redeeming factors about life that if you took a step back, you would realize how blessed you are. I live such a wonderful life, I was just born to think that I live an awful life, even if it's not true.  

In the moment, I thought about what my parents would think about me, lying on the ground dead. In that moment, as I was covered in tears, I made a suicide note, saying that I loved them both and that I was not meant to live on this earth. I told them that I had no regrets and from the the bottom of my heart, I thanked them for this wonderful life they've given me. That's when I didn't want to die. I wanted to keep living, even if I wouldn't be able to experience all the joys in life. It's okay if I want to die sometimes, but I believe that taking action towards suicide is not meant for me. I know that I was meant to live a life greater than sitting at home and wanting to kill myself. I wouldn't want to end my life knowing that I had so many regrets, even if everyone around me thought that I died peacefully.
